> **Note on file paths:** the original course material referenced files
> under `./data/`. Those files aren't part of this repo, so every example
> below either uses a built-in dataset or generates a small temp file on
> the fly — copy the pattern and point it at your own files.

# Built-in Data

R ships with sample datasets ready to use, no import needed.
```{r}
data(iris)
str(iris)
summary(iris)
ncol(iris)
```

Checking the class of every column, timed with base R (or use the `tictoc`
package's `tic()`/`toc()` for nicer output if you have it installed):
```{r}
dtypes <- c()
start <- Sys.time()
for (i in 1:ncol(iris)) {
  dtypes[i] <- class(iris[[i]])
}
print(Sys.time() - start)
unique(dtypes)
```

Loading a dataset from a package without loading the whole package:
```{r}
data("spam", package = "kernlab")
str(spam[1:5])
```

# CSV Files

Three common ways to read a CSV, from least to most modern:

* `read.csv()` from base R
```{r}
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(iris, tmp, row.names = FALSE)

dta <- read.csv(tmp)
head(dta, 3)
```
Notice `Species` comes back as `character` — pass `stringsAsFactors = TRUE`
to `read.csv()` if you want it as a factor instead.

* `read_csv()` from `readr` (loaded together with `tidyverse`)
```{r message=FALSE}
library(readr)
dta <- read_csv(tmp)
head(dta, 3)
```
Always check the messages/warnings `read_csv()` prints — they usually flag
real issues worth fixing.

* `import()` from `rio`, which auto-detects the file type
```{r message=FALSE}
library(rio)
head(import(tmp), 2)
unlink(tmp)
```

## Excel files

`rio::import()` handles `.xlsx` the same way it handles CSV:
```{r message=FALSE}
tmp_xlsx <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
export(head(iris, 5), tmp_xlsx)
head(import(tmp_xlsx), 2)
unlink(tmp_xlsx)
```

## Exercise: import every CSV in a folder with a loop

```{r}
dir.create("demo_csv", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(head(iris, 3), "demo_csv/iris_part.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(head(mtcars, 3), "demo_csv/mtcars_part.csv", row.names = FALSE)

file_names <- dir("demo_csv", pattern = "\\.csv$")
file_names

data_list <- list()
for (f in file_names) {
  data_list[[f]] <- read.csv(file.path("demo_csv", f))
}
str(data_list)
unlink("demo_csv", recursive = TRUE)
```
